blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Sustainability in the supply chain means running a business that does not harm people or the planet. It also means a company can keep going for many years. It is about lower carbon emissions, less waste, ethical sourcing, and fair treatment of workers.

Customers, investors and regulators watch this more every year. A chain that ignores sustainability slowly becomes more expensive, more risky, and harder to defend.

The good news is simple: many green choices also save money in the long run. A greener supply chain is not only good ethics. It is also good business.

items.q: What does sustainability in the supply chain mean?
options: Opening new offices in many countries
Running a business that does not harm people or the planet
items.why: "Sustainability in the supply chain means running a business that does not harm people or the planet."

items.q: According to the text, what is sustainability about?
options: Lower carbon emissions, less waste, ethical sourcing, and fair treatment
items.why: O texto lista: "lower carbon emissions, less waste, ethical sourcing, and fair treatment of workers."

items.q: Who watches sustainability more every year?
items.why: "Customers, investors and regulators watch this more every year."

items.q: What happens to a chain that ignores sustainability?
options: It becomes more expensive, more risky, and harder to defend
items.why: "A chain that ignores sustainability slowly becomes more expensive, more risky, and harder to defend."

items.q: The author would most likely AGREE that…
options: Waste is not a real problem
Green choices are only a cost and never help business
Sustainability can be good for ethics and for money
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz que muitas escolhas verdes "save money in the long run" e que é "good business".

blocks.instruction: Ouça Charlotte apresentando a revisão de sustentabilidade ao conselho. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Good morning, everyone. Thank you for your time. This is our first sustainability review, and I will keep it simple.

Our biggest customer now wants real data. They ask about our carbon emissions, our waste, and how we treat our workers. This is new for us. In the past, we only talked about price and speed. Today we must talk about the planet too.

I have some good news. Last year we cut waste in two of our sites. This saved money. It also made our teams proud. So a green choice is not always a cost. Sometimes it helps the business.

But I want to be honest. We do not measure everything yet. We should measure our carbon footprint first. Then we can set clear targets. Without data, we are only guessing.

My plan is simple. First, we collect the numbers. Second, we share them with our customer. Third, we choose two or three small changes for this year. Small steps add up over time. Thank you.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What is Charlotte presenting?
options: A plan to close two sites
items.why: "This is our first sustainability review."

items.q: What does the biggest customer want now?
options: Real data on emissions, waste and workers
items.why: "They ask about our carbon emissions, our waste, and how we treat our workers."

items.q: What good news does Charlotte share?
options: Cutting waste at two sites saved money
The company opened a new market
items.why: "Last year we cut waste in two of our sites. This saved money."

items.q: Why does Charlotte say "Without data, we are only guessing"?
options: Because good decisions need real numbers first
Because the team is too small
Because the customer is not important
items.why: Inferência: ela quer medir o carbono antes de definir metas — sem dados, não há base para decidir.

items.q: How would you best describe Charlotte's message?
options: Only about profit, not the planet
Honest and practical, with small clear steps
items.why: Inferência: ela admite que faltam dados, mas propõe passos pequenos e claros.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Our trucks produce too much carbon emissions." Carbon emissions are…
items.why: Carbon emissions = emissões de carbono, gases que prejudicam o ar.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "We throw away too much paper. We must cut our ___."
items.why: Waste = desperdício. Cortar o desperdício é o que faz sentido aqui.

items.q: "We buy only from farms with ethical sourcing." Ethical sourcing means…
options: buying in a fair and responsible way
items.why: Ethical sourcing = compras éticas, comprar de forma justa e responsável.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "A green choice can cost more today but save money in the ___."
items.why: Long run = longo prazo. "In the long run" = ao longo do tempo.

items.q: "The regulator asked for our sustainability report." A regulator is…
options: an official body that makes and checks rules
items.why: Regulator = regulador, órgão que cria e fiscaliza regras.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões sobre sustentabilidade. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The board still has to sign off on the new green plan." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We will roll out the new recycling plan site by site." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar aos poucos, por etapas.

items.q: "Some managers pushed back on the extra costs." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar.

items.q: "The team promised to cut waste but never followed through." They…
options: did not finish what they promised
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "Small changes will not move the needle unless we measure them." Move the needle means to…
items.why: Move the needle = fazer diferença perceptível.
